key_insight: Explicitly align image pixels to 3D geometry during generation so that the synthesized 3D asset is pixel-faithful to the input image, resolving ambiguous 2D→3D associations that hurt fidelity.
problem_solved: Addresses low pixel-level fidelity in image-to-3D generation caused by implicit or weak 2D–3D correspondences in existing 3D-native generators.
method: Introduce a pixel-alignment mechanism that maps image pixels (or pixel features) to positions on the generated 3D surface, creating explicit 2D→3D correspondences.
Condition a 3D-native generator on these pixel-aligned features so geometry and appearance are synthesized in canonical space but grounded to input pixels.
Enforce image consistency during training (e.g., reprojection/photometric and perceptual constraints) to preserve fine details and color fidelity.
impact: Enables much higher-fidelity, image-consistent 3D assets from single images—useful for content creation, AR/VR, and downstream vision tasks that require pixel-accurate geometry and appearance.
visual_elements: Before/After comparison: two rendered 3D assets from the same input image showing improved pixel-level fidelity.
Schematic diagram: pixel-alignment pipeline illustrating image → pixel features → mapping onto 3D surface → 3D generator.
Reprojection overlay: input image with reprojected generated 3D render to visualize pixel-to-3D correspondence and residuals.
Quantitative bar chart: fidelity metrics (e.g., pixel-wise error, perceptual score) comparing Pixal3D vs baselines.
paper_authors: Dong-Yang Li, Wang Zhao, Yuxin Chen, Wenbo Hu, Meng-Hao Guo
